free_tier.stated: No storage. Free, no account, no card. Public relays are rate-limited per connection but the rate limits are deliberately unpublished. The paid Shared tier is the only one with published figures: 100 GB relayed egress/month then $0.09/GB, 5 MB/s, 10,000 concurrent connections.

egress.terms: Free public relays, rate-limited. Self-hosting a relay is free and unlimited (open licence). The cost moves to your own bandwidth.

record.interface_detail: QUIC over TLS 1.3; Rust crate `iroh`, bindings for other languages
record.tooling: `iroh` crate; relay is a library, not a service with an upload endpoint
record.chaining: This is SIGNALLING, not relaying, in the normal case: 'roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a fallback'. The relay carries bytes only when hole punching fails, which is what makes the free tier viable at all.
record.limits_note: Not a storage provider. Only relayed bytes hit the operator, hence the per-connection rate limit rather than a byte quota.
record.reliability_note: 'The exact rate limits aren't published today, as they get tuned as needed' and 'Do not rely on it for production workloads'. The free tier is explicitly capacity-unstable by design.

evidence.proved: 'In practice, roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a fallback'; relays are stateless and cannot read traffic (QUIC/TLS 1.3)
'The exact rate limits aren't published today, as they get tuned as needed ... applied per connection'; 'Do not rely on it for production workloads'
Free: 'Rate limited' / 'Variable'; Pro $19/mo: 10,000 connections, shared relays, 5 MB/s; Dedicated $199/mo/region: unlimited
'100 GB of relay egress per month, then $0.09/GB'; 'A 5 MB/s rate limit'
worked example: 2,000 users x 10 GB/mo; 'if 98% of the traffic could travel directly ... only the remaining 2% (400 GB) would pass through'

record.notes: No storage. Free, no account, no card. Public relays are rate-limited per connection but the rate limits are deliberately unpublished. The paid Shared tier is the only one with published figures: 100 GB relayed egress/month then $0.09/GB, 5 MB/s, 10,000 concurrent connections.
record.binding_note: one stream is shaped, and aggregate throughput is the shaped rate times the number of streams

card.summary: 0 bytes of storage. Free plan = public relays in US/EU/Singapore, 7-day metrics retention, no auth, rate-limited traffic, no uptime guarantee.

record.category: Hosted coordination service (relays + metrics + diagnostics) — NOT storage

free_tier.stated: 0 bytes of storage. Free plan = public relays in US/EU/Singapore, 7-day metrics retention, no auth, rate-limited traffic, no uptime guarantee.

retention.stated: Free plan = public relays in US/EU/Singapore, 7-day metrics retention, no auth, rate-limited traffic, no uptime guarantee

record.interface_detail: Dashboard at services.iroh.computer + `iroh-services` crate; account is username + email + password.
record.tooling: `iroh_services::Client` pushes endpoint metrics on an interval; net-diagnostics can dial back into your endpoint (requires granting `Caps::net_diagnostics_get_any()`).
record.chaining: Free tier covers signalling and discovery for an unlimited number of endpoints. Which is exactly the part a self-hosted origin needs. It contributes nothing to bytes at rest or bytes served.
record.limits_note: Relay only. There is no pinning service, no blob hosting, no object storage SKU anywhere in n0's product line. The entire product is coordination plus egress.
record.reliability_note: Free tier requires an account only to see metrics; the relays themselves need no account at all.

evidence.proved: plan table: Free/Pro $19/Dedicated $199 per region/Enterprise; rows are Connections, Relays, Rate limit, Egress, Auth, Custom DNS, Metrics, Support. No storage row exists.
Public free / Cloud $19+ / Open Source self-host. 'Hosting' here means relays and discovery.
